subject: Post-call: Security questionnaire initiation + archive/erase window clarification
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj@cardioscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Security questionnaire initiation + archive/erase window clarification

Hi Raj / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the context on CardioScale's telemetry and retention needs. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get the vendor security questionnaire moving and confirm deletion/backup SLAs for procurement: 

Call recap (short):
- Use case: anomaly detection on aggregated telemetry + clinical metadata for product analytics (PHI scope flagged).
- Compliance requirements: HIPAA baseline + GDPR for EU customers; you indicated a stronger audit retention requirement for certain records.
- Deployment preference: hosted with VPC peering is preferred, but you may evaluate a Private (customer-managed) deployment if controls require it.

Asks / next steps for procurement/security:
1) Can you confirm the exact log/telemetry retention requirement you need for audit-grade records (you mentioned 7 years as a possible upper bound)?
2) What is your desired deletion SLA after a customer/record-level erase request (e.g., immediate, 30 days, 90 days)?
3) For backups and snapshots, do you treat snapshots as "recoverable" data that must be erased within the same window as primary data, or can they be retained under a longer contractual retention with documented restore processes?
4) Please upload the completed vendor security questionnaire (we've attached our template) or let us know if you'd prefer we complete your questionnaire first.

What we can provide immediately:
- Redwood can share a SOC 2 readiness summary and Type I report now; Type II is available for customers under NDA / VDR (we can grant access).
- Baseline behavior: activity logs (API/auth events) are available in hot storage for 90 days by default, backups are retained for 365 days in our standard plan. Custom retention and longer backup retention are available as contract options.
- Deletion process: soft-delete + orchestration to remove primary and cached data within 30 days by default; backup/snapshot erase windows depend on snapshot lifecycle but can be negotiated.

I've attached our SQ template to speed things up. If helpful, Ben (cc'd) from Security can jump on a brief call to walk the team through the evidence we can provide.

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire-RD-20270403.xlsx (spreadsheet), call-recording-20270403.mp3 (recording stub)

Next suggested step: please confirm the retention windows above and drop your completed SQ back here. If you want us to start the VDR access process for SOC 2 artifacts, say the word and we'll open a read-only folder.

Thanks —

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Raj Singh <raj@cardioscale.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@cardioscale.com>, security@cardioscale.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Security questionnaire initiation + archive/erase window clarification

Thanks Jasmine — great summary. Quick answers from our side so you can triage: 

- Retention requirement: for audit-grade telemetry tied to clinical events we need up to 7 years; for non-clinical analytics traces 12–18 months is sufficient.
- Deletion SLA: for patient/PHI erasure we need confirmation that primary data will be removed within 30 days of request; for backups/snapshots we accept a contractual exception but prefer a maximum of 180 days for snapshots containing PHI with documented restore controls.
- Backups vs snapshots: snapshots are considered recoverable and thus we want them covered by the same erasure obligation unless we sign a longer retention addendum.
- SOC 2: we need to see SOC 2 Type II or, if not available, an official timeline for Type II and current Type I.

I've attached our internal security questionnaire to this reply (we usually ask vendors to complete it). If you can start by filling the high-priority sections (data flows, encryption, key management, retention and backups, incident response), that would speed procurement.

Two quick asks: 1) is there a named security contact we can work with for evidence collection? 2) can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in the Private deployment?

Thanks —
Raj
VP, Platform & Security
CardioScale

Attachment: CardioScale-SQ-20270404.xlsx (their SQ template)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj@cardioscale.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@cardioscale.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Security questionnaire initiation + archive/erase window clarification

Hi Raj / Priya —

Appreciate the quick detail — wanted to chime in with concrete answers and an offer to move evidence into a VDR. High-level answers below; happy to iterate on contract language for any exceptions: 

1) SOC 2 status:
- Current: Redwood holds a SOC 2 Type I report (control design) and a readiness pack for Type II.
- Next steps: we can grant CardioScale read-only VDR access to the Type I report and our readiness artifacts today. Type II is on our roadmap and we can provide an estimated delivery quarter (we'll include a formal target date under NDA).

2) Retention / backups / snapshots:
- Default: hot telemetry (searchable activity/trace logs) = 90 days.
- Standard backup snapshot retention = 365 days. Snapshots are treated as recoverable copies; they require a separate erase process.
- Contracting option: we can set longer primary or backup retention up to 7 years by amendment; for PHI this is scoped and priced as an enterprise option.

3) Deletion SLA / erase window:
- Default erase flow: soft-delete triggers immediate unlinking from active indices, orchestration to remove primary and caches within 30 days.
- Backup/snapshot erase: available as a contract clause — default max snapshot purge is 90days, but we can extend to 180 days for PHI with documented controls; 7-year snapshot retention is available under long-term archiving addendum.

4) Customer-managed keys / Private deployment:
- Yes — Private supports KMS integration (customer-managed KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest keys. Hosted offering supports CMK in select regions; we can include this explicitly in SOW.

Next steps we recommend:
- Jasmine: please open the CardioScale SQ (attached by Raj) in our tracker and assign high-priority questions to Security (Ben / Neha).
- I'll open a read-only VDR link for CardioScale and upload the SOC 2 Type I + readiness summary.
- Offer: 30-minute evidence review call this week with our Security team to walk through the VDR and any redlines — use the Calendly link if helpful.

Attachments we'll push to the VDR: redwood-soc2-readiness-summary.pdf, redwood-logging-architecture-diagram.pdf (evidence stub).

Ben Carter
Security Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
